source.title: From Atoms to Trees: Building a Structured Feature Forest with Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Yi-Fan Luo; Yang Zhan; Jie-Dong Jiang; Tian-Yang Liu; Ming-Rui Wu; Zhen-Nan Zhou; Bin Dong

page_placements.theme: SAE architectures that build in a hierarchy
Absorption depends on the SAE objective and architecture, not only on size or sparsity

record.tranche_reason: The study measures parent-child activation alignment and semantic relations across SAE dictionary levels, using a jointly trained hierarchical SAE and metrics different from the original feature-splitting demonstrations.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates hierarchical alignment, co-activation, automated semantic judgments, and sibling-feature geometry. It also reports an absorption benchmark. Related benchmark metrics such as reconstruction, sparse probing, SCR, and RAVEL are not included because they do not measure the claimed splitting or hierarchy.
record.test_reason: The independently trained JumpReLU SAE baseline (2048 to 16384 latents, post-hoc parent assignment) measures how well naturally split features nest, in Gemma 2 2B and Qwen3 4B. It reports parent-given-child and child-given-parent co-activation and Hamming distance (Table 3), plus SAEBench absorption across dictionary sizes (Table 1). HSAE values come from an objective built to enforce the hierarchy, so they are the authors' own method and do not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also frame feature splitting as direct evidence of a hierarchy in the model, not an obstacle. They report that HSAE reduces absorption, which they link to Matryoshka SAEs. They acknowledge persistent parent-child misalignment of unclear origin.
record.recipe_differences: HSAE jointly trains JumpReLU SAEs at increasing dictionary sizes, updates parent-child assignments during training, and uses a parent-child constraint loss plus random feature perturbation; its comparison baseline trains independent SAEs and aligns them post hoc.
record.method_sensitivity: Target sparsity changes alignment: the Gemma 2 layer-13 alignment metrics weaken at target L0 80 and 100 relative to 50. Constraint weight and perturbation rate trade off hierarchy alignment against variance explained, but the text gives no numerical values for those settings.

fits_no_version.finding: A hierarchy-enforcing training objective (HSAE) roughly halves SAEBench absorption at 16k latents versus independent SAEs (0.078 vs 0.156). The authors link this to Matryoshka SAEs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Objectives that build in nested or hierarchical structure reduce feature absorption, though it is not eliminated and still grows with dictionary size.

fits_no_version.finding: UMAP shows activations triggering HSAE sibling features lying closer than those of unrelated features. This is qualitative, with no baseline comparison, and siblings are assigned by encoder similarity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sibling features in a learned hierarchy correspond to nearby regions of model activation space.

record.problems: The hierarchy is explicitly encouraged by the training objective, so the results do not by themselves establish that ordinary SAEs naturally recover the same hierarchy. Geometric evidence is qualitative UMAP visualization. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates or numerical values for several figures, and its absorption benchmark does not identify the specific takeover cases described in V4.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 results for variance explained, AutoInterp, RAVEL, SCR, and sparse probing were omitted because they do not directly measure the claimed splitting or hierarchy. Figure 7 similarity-metric comparisons and Figure 8 hyperparameter plots were omitted because the text reports no numerical results for them; their results do not directly test the claim’s feature-splitting pattern.

untested.parts: Decoder-direction proximity of child to parent is not measured. No qualitative examples of splits in the baseline (independent) SAEs are shown; the case studies are HSAE.
No open SAE releases. Only own-trained JumpReLU SAEs on Gemma 2 2B and Qwen3 4B.
No quantitative geometry of baseline feature families. The UMAP evidence covers only HSAE siblings.
Entire version: decomposition of larger latents and novel latents are not tested.
Whether splitting is an artifact of the objective is not tested. No Matryoshka comparison. The authors assert the opposite interpretation without a test.

missing.what: Numeric LLM-judge rate of valid parent-child relations for the post-hoc baseline hierarchy (and HSAE)

record.verdict_notes: The only version-relevant evidence is the independent-SAE baseline; HSAE is engineered to produce the hierarchy. The record's V1/V2/V3 'supports' labels rested on HSAE beating the baseline, which is a comparison of the authors' method, not a test. Hamming distance units are unstated. Section 2 cites results from the original sources; those are not rows.

versions.untested_parts: It does not directly measure whether parent and child decoder directions are nearby, or independently establish that naturally occurring larger-dictionary features partition a smaller feature’s inputs.
Tests Gemma 2 2B and Qwen3 4B and several Gemma layers, but not open SAE releases or a broad set of large models.
The reported geometry is qualitative UMAP evidence about sibling activation clusters; it does not quantitatively establish nested directional geometry across a broad range of models.
Measures parent-child co-activation and an SAE absorption benchmark, but does not directly establish the specific takeover cases described in the claim.
Does not test whether larger latents decompose into combinations of smaller latents or whether larger dictionaries add novel latents.
Does not test whether splitting is an artifact of the sparsity objective or compare against Matryoshka SAEs.

source_check.notes: All values match Tables 1 and 3; baselines bear on versions, HSAE is the authors' method. T3 pairs link latents in adjacent-size independent SAEs by post-hoc similarity: they measure nesting, not within-SAE absorption, so their V4 links are doubtful. Absorption is reported only for Gemma 2 2B L13 at L0 about 50. No code, no uncertainty. The App C judge prompt is quoted method text, not instructions.

statements.correction: The study compares each parent's activation with the logical OR of its children (Hamming distance; mismatches in both directions). Baseline: 34.6 (Gemma 2 2B L6); 36.1/61.9/78.9 (L13, L0 50/80/100); 30.6 (L20); 46.4 (Qwen3 4B L18). HSAE is lower. P(parent|child) 0.309-0.729 is a containment measure, not coverage.
statements.problem: P(parent|child) measures children firing outside the parent, not whether children cover the parent's inputs. 'No study quantifies union coverage' misses this study's Hamming distance between the parent and the logical OR of its children.

statements.correction: Table 3, Gemma 2 2B layer 13 baseline Hamming distance: 36.1 at L0 50, 61.9 at L0 80, 78.9 at L0 100.
statements.problem: Says the L0 50 Hamming value is cut off, but the text gives it.
Context, not an error: Sec 4.6 claims the hierarchy is inherently represented in the LLM's activation geometry, from a qualitative UMAP of HSAE siblings only.

statements.correction: Baseline P(parent|child) for post-hoc pairs across adjacent-size SAEs: 0.651 (Gemma 2 2B L6); 0.662/0.634/0.619 (L13, L0 50/80/100); 0.729 (L20); 0.309 (Qwen3 4B L18). SAEBench absorption is reported only for Gemma 2 2B L13 at L0 about 50 (Table 1). The paper does not frame co-activation as absorption.
statements.problem: Treats cross-size parent-child co-activation as absorption. The pairs link a latent in one SAE to a latent in the next larger, independently trained SAE, assigned post hoc by similarity. The study reports absorption only at L0 about 50. Baseline pairs are not 'learned'.

statements.correction: Qwen3 4B layer 18 baseline P(parent|child) = 0.309 (HSAE 0.347), for post-hoc pairs across independently trained SAEs. No absorption score is reported for Qwen3 4B.
statements.problem: 0.309 is cross-size parent-given-child co-activation, not an absorption level. The listed differences omit this metric difference.

statements.correction: Gemma 2 2B L13 baseline P(parent|child), parent and child in adjacent-size independent SAEs: 0.662 (L0 50), 0.634 (L0 80), 0.619 (L0 100). SAEBench absorption is reported only at L0 about 50 (Table 1).
statements.problem: 'Parent misses worse at higher L0' is set against absorption-vs-L0 results. In this study it is cross-size co-activation of post-hoc pairs, and the study has no absorption result at L0 80/100.

statements.correction: This study's absorption evidence is SAEBench Absorption (Chanin et al. 2024) on Gemma 2 2B L13 (Table 1). The T3 parent-child pairs (similarity-assigned; learned only in HSAE) measure nesting across dictionary sizes.
statements.problem: Lists the T3 rows as a non-first-letter exception in absorption evidence. The T3 rows measure cross-size co-activation, not absorption. The baseline pairs are assigned post hoc, not learned. The study's absorption number is SAEBench's Absorption metric.
